# 3. Transport layer (internal/transport/rest) design decisions

## Status

Accepted

## Context

This records the transport/auth decisions made while wiring up
`internal/transport/rest` and `cmd/wordgame`.

## Decisions

### 1. `UserID` is external, read from `X-User-Id`, never generated by this service

The README's game protocol has no concept of accounts or login — a caller is
just "whoever is playing". `X-User-Id` is treated as already authenticated by
whatever sits in front of this service.

### 2. maxkit's default auth middleware is used as-is, including a hardcoded role

`app.Serve` always wraps the handler with maxkit's standard auth middleware.
Its default (service-to-service stub) mode requires every request to carry
`Authorization: Bearer <stub-token>` plus `X-User-Id` and `X-User-Role`
(parsed into `admin`/`client`). This service has no actual notion of roles —
every caller is a game player — so callers are required to send
`X-User-Role: client` on every request, purely to satisfy maxkit's header
parsing.

**The simulated topology behind this:** this service is written as if it sits
behind an API gateway, not as the internet-facing edge itself. The imagined
flow is: a frontend authenticates a player elsewhere and receives a user JWT
(plus a refresh token, for session renewal); it sends that user JWT on each
game request; an API gateway in front of `wordgame` verifies that JWT, then
calls this service using its own separate service-to-service credential —
translating the verified player identity into the `X-User-Id`/`X-User-Role`
headers this service trusts, per `Authenticator.Middleware`'s own doc comment
("trusting that an upstream gateway resolved them"). The
`Authorization: Bearer <stub-token>` this service actually checks stands in
for that gateway's service credential, not the player's own JWT — this
service never sees or validates the player's token directly, matching how a
gateway-fronted internal service normally works. None of that gateway or
JWT-issuing machinery is actually built here; it's simulated only to the
extent of matching the header contract it would produce.

**Rationale:** this is a deliberate, accepted mismatch with the README's
bare `curl -X POST .../new` examples, rather than a hidden one.

### 3. No shared `internal/transport` package

DTOs (`GameStateDTO`, `GuessRequest`) live directly in
`internal/transport/rest`, not a parent `internal/transport` package, since
REST is the only transport this service has. A shared package would be
justified if a second transport (gRPC, a CLI) were ever added and needed the
same wire shapes.
